# Q1/Q2 journal-readiness audit

*Generated by `scripts/q1_q2_audit.py` at 2026-08-28T07:20:22Z from stored artefacts at commit `886dc84205a3`. No experiment was run. Every number is re-derived from `results/`; where a document disagrees with an artefact, the artefact wins.*

## Verdict

### MAJOR REVISION REQUIRED — most of it now applied

The study is internally sound, unusually well controlled, and its central statistical claim survives scrutiny. When this audit was first written the paper was not submittable, for three reasons all fixable from data already on disk: a decisive result was missing from the manuscript, a power claim was wrong, and 1,050 completed cells were never analysed.

**Status of the four P0 items, re-checked against the artefacts on this run:**

| P0 item | status |
|---|---|
| Baselines beat every RL arm, unreported | **RESOLVED** — the full method ranking now opens Results and appears in the abstract |
| MDE wrong; post-hoc power argument | **RESOLVED** — both SDs reported, the post-hoc argument removed, jackknife and Wilcoxon added |
| 1,050 sensitivity cells unanalysed | **RESOLVED** — `results/sensitivity_analysis.json`; the reward-weight ablation turned out vacuous on the primary endpoint and that is now reported as a finding |
| Mechanism asserted, not tested | **PARTIALLY RESOLVED** — `results/mechanism_analysis.json` identifies the dispatch effect from stored data; the registered epoch-level form of H1b still needs the per-epoch forecast and remains open |

The verdict stays at MAJOR REVISION because the remaining objections are not editorial: the RL arms lose to a threshold heuristic, the budget confound is unresolved until the registered follow-up completes, and the endpoint depends on unvalidated simulator components. Those bound what the paper can claim regardless of how well it is written.

## Finding 1 (CRITICAL) — the baselines beat every RL arm, and the manuscript never says so

Mean `left_behind_fraction`, lower is better, seed-level means:

| method | normal | surge | disruption | combined |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `heuristic_threshold` | 0.00491 | 0.01184 | 0.01005 | 0.01680 |
| `milp_static` | 0.00491 | 0.01187 | 0.01005 | 0.01705 |
| `ppo_point` | 0.01119 | 0.01794 | 0.01635 | 0.02324 |
| `ppo_placebo` | 0.01657 | 0.02316 | 0.02019 | 0.02684 |
| `fixed_timetable` | 0.01879 | 0.02550 | 0.02207 | 0.02864 |

| `milp_rolling` | 0.02384 | 0.02932 | 0.02690 | 0.03205 |
| `ppo_uq` **<-- proposed** | 0.02429 | 0.03168 | 0.02563 | 0.03219 |
| `ppo_uq_single_obj` | 0.13543 | 0.14694 | 0.13658 | 0.14651 |

Mean `total_reward` — the scalar objective every RL arm was trained to maximise, higher is better:

| method | normal | surge | disruption | combined |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `heuristic_threshold` | -737.0 | -847.4 | -806.4 | -922.2 |
| `milp_static` | -746.6 | -857.3 | -815.9 | -935.5 |
| `ppo_point` | -843.5 | -956.0 | -915.1 | -1037.0 |
| `ppo_placebo` | -921.3 | -1035.4 | -970.9 | -1091.7 |
| `fixed_timetable` | -924.9 | -1042.3 | -969.3 | -1092.5 |
| `ppo_uq_noavail` | -997.7 | -1123.1 | -1016.0 | -1144.8 |
| `milp_rolling` | -1029.0 | -1135.6 | -1073.6 | -1175.1 |
| `ppo_uq` **<-- proposed** | -1026.3 | -1157.0 | -1050.2 | -1173.2 |
| `ppo_uq_single_obj` | -5848.1 | -6334.8 | -5867.4 | -6321.3 |

In **every one of the four scenarios**, on **both** the primary endpoint and the training objective, `heuristic_threshold` and `milp_static` beat every reinforcement-learning arm. The proposed method `ppo_uq` (0.03168 under surge) is 2.7x worse than a tuned threshold heuristic (0.01184), and worse than the **fixed timetable** (0.02550) — that is, worse than not adapting at all.

`results/figures/fig01_primary_endpoint.png` plots all nine methods, so this was always visible in the figure while appearing nowhere in the prose. **Now resolved**: the ranking opens the Results section and is stated in the abstract. The finding is kept here because it remains the paper's dominant substantive weakness, not because it is still unreported.

**This does not invalidate H1.** The H1 contrast is `ppo_uq` versus `ppo_point`, both RL arms, and it stands. What it invalidates is the framing: the paper is currently written as though the interesting question is which RL arm wins, when the stored results say the RL approach as configured loses to a threshold rule.

It also sharpens the A-05 confound past the point the manuscript admits. A PPO configuration that cannot beat a tuned threshold heuristic is more plausibly **undertrained** than informative about uncertainty. The single-objective arm makes this concrete: seed 104 diverged to 0.819 left-behind fraction, two orders of magnitude off its siblings, which is a training-stability failure, not a policy preference.

## Finding 2 (CRITICAL) — the power claim is wrong, and it is the wrong kind of argument

| quantity | value |
|---|---:|
| between-seed SD assumed by the R-1 gate (from the pilot) | 0.005298 |
| **realised** SD of the confirmatory paired differences | **0.011269** |
| ratio | **2.13x** |
| MDE quoted in every document (pilot SD) | 0.005909 |
| MDE recomputed on the realised SD | **0.012717** |
| observed effect | 0.013742 |
| observed / quoted MDE — the "2.3x" claim | 2.33x |
| observed / **realised** MDE | **1.08x** |

Two separate problems.

**The pilot underestimated the between-seed SD by 2.13x.** Four pilot seeds is a thin basis for a variance estimate, and the variance came in more than double. Recomputed honestly, the observed effect is 1.08x the minimum detectable effect, not 2.33x. The study was *marginally* powered for the effect it found, not comfortably powered.

**The argument itself is a post-hoc power argument**, which is a recognised fallacy. Once a test has rejected, comparing the observed effect to a minimum detectable effect adds nothing: the p-value and the confidence interval already carry the evidence, and observed power is a deterministic function of the p-value. A statistically literate reviewer will flag the sentence *"the observed effect is 2.3x the minimum detectable effect, so this is a conclusive negative rather than an artefact of low power"* twice — once for the arithmetic and once for the logic.

The honest replacement is available and *stronger*, because it is a real robustness result rather than a rhetorical one:

- The null is rejected: Holm-adjusted p = 0.00774114.
- The 95% BCa CI is [0.006570, 0.018523], excluding zero and lying entirely above the SESOI of 0.0020.
- A distribution-free cross-check agrees: Wilcoxon signed-rank p = 0.005859.
- **Leave-one-seed-out**: the worst case across all 10 jackknife replicates is p = 0.01021 (dropping seed 107), Holm-adjusted 0.02043 — still significant. The conclusion does not rest on any single training seed.
- 9 of 10 seeds favour `ppo_point`.

The same correction propagates to the SESOI limitation, and makes it worse: detecting the SESOI of 0.0020 needs n = 69 at the pilot SD but **n = 305** at the realised SD.

## Finding 3 (CRITICAL) — 1,050 completed cells are never analysed

`1,050` episodes were computed for the two registered sensitivity experiments, and **no test, table or figure reports them**:

| experiment | cells | appears in the analysis? |
|---|---:|---|
| EXP-SENS-002 (`od_cbd_attracted`) | 150 | **no** |
| EXP-SENS-002 (`od_distance_decay`) | 150 | **no** |
| EXP-SENS-002 (`od_uniform_downstream`) | 150 | **no** |
| EXP-SENS-001 (`weights_w_cost`) | 200 | **no** |
| EXP-SENS-001 (`weights_w_service`) | 200 | **no** |
| EXP-SENS-001 (`weights_w_unmet_heavy`) | 200 | **no** |

Experiment ids that produce a reported test: EXP-AVAIL-001, EXP-MO-001, EXP-UQ-001, EXP-UQ-002, EXP-UQ-003. `EXP-SENS-001` and `EXP-SENS-002` are absent from both families.

This matters because the manuscript **claims they do the work**:

> *"OD-model sensitivity (EXP-SENS-002) and reward-weight sensitivity (EXP-SENS-001) test whether the ordering survives the synthetic OD assumption and alternative scalarisations."* — `docs/manuscript_draft.md`

> *"EXP-SENS-002 re-runs the comparison under three OD variants specifically to test whether the conclusion is OD-dependent. The result is reported as OD-robust or OD-dependent according to what those cells show."* — `docs/final_peer_review.md`

Neither was true as written: the cells existed, the analysis did not.

**Now resolved.** `scripts/sensitivity_analysis.py` analyses them, separately from the confirmatory artefact so the immutable study is untouched. The registered direction holds under all three OD models. The reward-weight arm turned out to be **vacuous on the primary endpoint** — re-scoring a frozen policy under a different weighting changes no action, so `left_behind_fraction` is identical per seed across all three weightings and only `total_reward` differs — which is itself a finding the manuscript now reports rather than an analysis it can lean on.

## Finding 4 (MAJOR) — the mechanism claim is asserted, not tested

The manuscript and `final_results.md` both attribute the degradation to **under-dispatching**, inferred from lower energy and cost alongside worse service. The registry contains a hypothesis that would test this directly:

> **H1b / EXP-UQ-004:** *the uncertainty-aware policy's dispatch rate increases with forecast dispersion after conditioning on the forecast mean; the point policy's does not.*

`docs/paper_traceability.md` records H1b as **NOT YET TESTED** — `results/mechanism_analysis.json` does not exist. So the paper's causal story about *why* the uncertainty channel hurts rests on an aggregate correlation across three metrics, not on the registered mechanism test.

**Now partially resolved.** `results/mechanism_analysis.json` settles the aggregate question from stored data: the calibrated sigma reduces dispatch volume sharply in every scenario while a placebo sigma of identical marginal distribution does not, and at matched volume the uncertainty arm leaves more idle epochs and reaches a larger peak queue than a fixed timetable. So both under-dispatching *and* mis-timing are present, and the effect is attributable to the sigma being informative rather than to the extra inputs.

The registered epoch-level form of H1b — dispatch rate against forecast dispersion, conditional on the forecast mean — still has no artefact, because the stored cells do not carry the per-epoch forecast. It is documented as open rather than quietly dropped.

## Finding 5 (MAJOR) — no baseline comparison is statistically testable

Four registered hypotheses — H4, H5, H6, H6b, all of the form *adaptive RL outperforms <baseline>* — are recorded as **NOT YET TESTED** with *"no stored comparison"*. The reason is structural: the protocol fixes the training seed as the unit of analysis (section 8.2), and the baselines are deterministic and have no training seed, so each collapses to **n = 1**. The analysis correctly refuses to fabricate a test and reports differences of means instead.

The refusal is right; the design choice that forced it is questionable. A paired comparison across the 30 **evaluation** seeds is well defined — pair each baseline's per-day outcome against the RL arm's per-day outcome averaged over training seeds — and would give a legitimate inferential comparison at n = 30 days, with the training-seed variance handled by averaging rather than ignored. That analysis is not run.

Consequence: **the paper cannot make a single inferential claim about RL versus any baseline.** Given Finding 1, the descriptive comparison is unfavourable, so this reads as a convenient gap whether or not it was one.

## Finding 6 (MAJOR) — the unvalidated simulator quantities are exactly the ones the endpoint depends on

Simulator validation: validated = 4, partially validated = 3, not validatable = 7, mismatch = 0.

The not-validatable list is not a random sample of the model's internals:

- Train capacity / peak occupancy
- Station dwell-time distribution
- Passenger waiting behaviour (balking, patience)
- Origin-destination distribution
- Per-train trajectories and delays
- Energy consumption in physical units
- Operating cost in currency

`left_behind_fraction` is, definitionally, a function of train capacity and peak occupancy, dwell-time behaviour, passenger patience and balking, and the OD distribution. **Four of the seven unvalidated quantities are direct inputs to the primary endpoint.** What was validated — running time, round trips, headway, daily boardings — constrains the *supply* side, not the *crowding* side that the endpoint measures.

The defence is real but narrow: every arm faces identical conditions under common random numbers, so the *ordering* is internally valid. The *magnitude* — including the 77% relative degradation — is a property of an unvalidated crowding model and must not be quoted as an operational number.

## Finding 7 (MAJOR) — almost every stored result was produced from an uncommitted working tree

| manifest state | cells |
|---|---:|
| `provisional: true` and `git_dirty: true` | **7,609** |
| clean tree | 1 |
| no commit recorded at all (`git_commit: unknown`) | 559 |
| total manifests | 7,610 |

**7,609 of 7,610 cells** — every result in the study except a single audit re-run — were generated while the working tree had uncommitted changes. The manifests record a commit for 7,051 of them, but with `git_dirty: true` that commit does **not** determine the code that produced the result: a third party checking it out would be running different code from the one that ran.

The instrumentation deserves credit for recording this rather than hiding it — `provisional: true` is exactly the right flag and it is set correctly. The problem is that nothing downstream acts on it.

In particular, the reproducibility audit's `working tree clean` check inspects the tree **at audit time**, not at cell-production time. Because the results were committed before the final audit ran, that check now passes — while every cell it is vouching for was produced from an uncommitted state. The check is measuring the wrong moment, and its PASS is therefore not evidence for the property a reader would assume it certifies.

This is recoverable and does not invalidate any result. The code is now committed, the differences between the recorded commit and the final state are small and known, and the artefacts are all present. But the paper should not claim commit-level reproducibility for the stored results, and the audit check should be re-scoped to read the manifests.

## Minor findings

- **H3's support rests on one diverged seed.** `ppo_uq_single_obj` has a seed-level SD of 0.238 driven by seed 104. The direction is consistent, but the effect magnitude is not interpretable; report the median, not the mean.
- **H7 is mislabelled.** `paper_traceability.md` shows H7 as *NOT YET TESTED* when it was tested and came back non-significant. The verdict vocabulary conflates "no test" with "inconclusive test". The distinction matters here, because H7's own MDE is far above its observed effect, so it is genuinely inconclusive rather than untested.
- **`waiting_time_mean_s` is missing from the exploratory tables** although it is a stored column, while `waiting_time_p95_s` is reported. Unexplained metric selection invites a cherry-picking question that is trivially answered by reporting both.
- **`waiting_time_mean_s`** is likewise stored but unreported (see above).

## What survives the audit unchanged

These were checked against the artefacts and are correct:

- **The primary test.** Recomputed independently from `results/seed_level.parquet`: t = 3.85601, p = 0.00387057, matching the stored artefact to every printed digit.
- **Holm correction.** Two tests, p = 0.00387057 and 0.0117068; adjusted 0.00774114 and 0.0117068. Hand-recomputed: correct.
- **Endpoint direction.** Verified against metrics whose better-direction is opposite (`total_reward`, `energy_units`): the direction logic is right.
- **TOST.** Correctly *not* run: it is reserved for non-rejections, and the observed difference is 6.9x the SESOI.
- **Hodges-Lehmann and BCa.** Appropriate choices at n = 10; the normality check (Shapiro p = 0.6026) does not reject, so the paired t-test is also defensible, and the two agree.
- **No leakage, no seed contamination, no pilot data in confirmatory tests.** Verified structurally: pilot cells carry `variant='pilot'`, seed pools are disjoint, and the CRN stream builder takes no method argument.
- **Reproducibility machinery.** The audit reports PASS = 23, FAIL = 0, WARN = 1, SKIPPED = 0, the single warning being the regime-screen fallback, a property of the data rather than of the code. Hash-pinned dependencies, disjoint seed pools and script-rendered documents all hold. Finding 7 qualifies what this certifies, but the machinery itself is sound and is still the submission's strongest feature.

## Underclaims — results that deserve more emphasis than they get

1. **The degradation is large, not marginal.** 77% worse than the point-forecast arm on the primary endpoint. The manuscript reports the absolute difference and never the relative one.
2. **It is consistent across all four scenarios**, not a surge artefact: normal +0.01310, surge +0.01374, disruption +0.00928, combined +0.00895. Robustness of a negative result is evidence, and it is currently one line in an exploratory table.
3. **The jackknife result is genuinely strong** and is not reported at all: the conclusion survives dropping any single seed (worst Holm-adjusted p = 0.02043).
4. **The placebo ordering is graded**, which is more informative than a binary comparison: `ppo_point` 0.01794 < `ppo_placebo` 0.02316 < `ppo_uq` 0.03168. An uninformative channel of the same shape costs something; an informative one costs more. That pattern is hard to explain by dimensionality alone and deserves a paragraph.
5. **The pre-registration machinery is a contribution in itself** — a registry that code refuses to run against unless frozen, structural CRN, and documents rendered from artefacts so no number can be typed by hand. Most negative results are not this hard to dismiss.

## Likely reviewer objections

**Reviewer 1 — the applied transport reviewer.** *"Your Figure 1 shows a tuned threshold heuristic outperforming every learned policy in every scenario. Why is this not the headline? What does the paper contribute to metro operations if the recommended approach is beaten by a rule an operator could implement in an afternoon?"* This is the hardest objection and the manuscript currently has no answer, because it does not acknowledge the fact.

**Reviewer 2 — the machine-learning reviewer.** *"A PPO agent that cannot beat a threshold rule is undertrained. You froze one configuration at a fixed budget and concluded something about uncertainty representations. The result is about your optimiser, not about uncertainty."* Partly answerable — the placebo arm shows the *ordering among arms* is not a pure capacity artefact — but only partly, and not while the RL arms sit below the baselines.

**Reviewer 3 — the statistics reviewer.** *"Your pilot SD was off by a factor of two, your quoted MDE is therefore wrong, and you then use post-hoc power to argue your negative is conclusive. Also, four of your registered hypotheses have no test, and two registered sensitivity experiments have 1,050 cells and no analysis."* Every part of this is correct as the manuscript stands, and every part is fixable from existing data.

## Fatal concerns

**None.** No finding invalidates the experiment, the data, or the H1 conclusion. Every critical finding is a reporting or analysis defect over data that already exists.

The one framing that *would* be fatal is submitting this as a contribution to RL-based metro scheduling. As a pre-registered falsification study it is defensible; as a proposed method it is refuted by its own baselines.

## Recommended pre-registered follow-up study

**Not to be run now, and not to be added to this paper.** Running these after seeing the confirmatory result would convert a clean pre-registered study into a post-hoc one, which is a worse trade than any reviewer objection they would answer.

1. **Training-budget sweep** on `ppo_uq` and `ppo_point` across several timestep budgets, with the baselines fixed. This is the only experiment that can separate an information effect from an optimisation effect, and it directly answers Reviewer 2. It is now the *primary* open question, because Finding 1 shows the budget is inadequate in absolute terms and not merely relative to the arms.
2. **Sigma-scaling probe** — feed the channel a deliberately mis-scaled sigma (halved, doubled). Monotone response implicates magnitude rather than information.
3. **A reward weighting under which hedging should pay** — the current scalarisation rewards under-dispatch locally through the energy and cost terms.

A registered report is the right vehicle: the design is already written and the negative result is already in hand.

## Direct answers

**1. Can this study legitimately be submitted to a journal?** Yes, after the P0 revisions — and only as a falsification/negative-result study. Not as written.

**2. Strongest defensible contribution?** The experimental design: a placebo arm with identical dimensionality and marginal distribution, structural common random numbers, a registry the code refuses to run against unless frozen, and a seed-level unit of analysis. That combination is what makes the negative result hard to dismiss, and it is rare in this literature.

**3. Biggest weakness?** The RL arms lose to a tuned threshold heuristic in every scenario. This makes the practical contribution nil and makes the undertraining confound much more serious than the manuscript concedes.

**4. Biggest reviewer attack?** Reviewer 1's: the headline figure contradicts the framing, and the text does not mention it.

**5. Does the negative H1 result remain scientifically valuable?** Yes. It is pre-registered, placebo-controlled, consistent across four scenarios, robust to dropping any seed, and it contradicts a widely held intuition. Its value is bounded by the budget confound — it says *this* channel did not help *this* controller at *this* budget — but within those bounds it is solid, and the bounds are stateable.

**6. Is another experiment genuinely necessary before submission?** **No.** Every critical and major finding is fixable by analysing data already on disk. The training-budget experiment is necessary for the *interpretation* to be settled, but running it now would compromise the pre-registration; it belongs in the follow-up, with the limitation stated plainly here.

**7. Which improvements need no new experiment?** All of the P0 items: analysing the 1,050 sensitivity cells, adding the baseline comparison to the text, correcting the MDE and removing the post-hoc power argument, adding the jackknife robustness result, testing the dispatch mechanism from the stored `inductions` column, and adding an eval-seed-paired baseline comparison. Every one reads from `results/`.
